title: Two Sum
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
hint: Use a HashMap to store each number and its index. For each element, check if (target - element) exists in the map.
approach: Brute Force: O(n²) — check all pairs. Optimal: Single pass HashMap — store visited numbers, check complement exists in O(1).

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on the ith day. Maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy and a single day to sell.
hint: Track the minimum price seen so far. At each step, calculate profit = current - minPrice.
approach: One pass: Keep track of minPrice and maxProfit. For each price, update minPrice if smaller, else update maxProfit = max(maxProfit, price - minPrice).

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum and return its sum. (Kadane's Algorithm)
hint: At each index, decide: extend previous subarray or start fresh. currentSum = max(num, currentSum + num).
approach: Kadane's Algorithm: currentSum = max(nums[i], currentSum + nums[i]). maxSum = max(maxSum, currentSum). Reset when currentSum goes negative.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.
hint: Use a stack. Push opening brackets. For closing brackets, check if top of stack matches.
approach: Stack approach: Push '(', '{', '[' onto stack. For ')', '}', ']' — pop from stack and check if it's the matching opener. At end, stack must be empty.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
hint: Use sliding window with two pointers. Move right pointer, if char repeats move left pointer past the previous occurrence.
approach: Sliding Window + HashMap: Store last seen index of each char. When duplicate found, move left = max(left, lastSeen[char] + 1). Window size = right - left + 1.

title: Merge Intervals
description: Given an array of intervals, merge all overlapping intervals.
hint: Sort intervals by start time. Then iterate and merge if current start <= previous end.
approach: Sort by start time O(n log n). Iterate: if intervals overlap (curr.start <= prev.end), merge by updating end = max(prev.end, curr.end). Else add to result.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
hint: Water at index i = min(maxLeft, maxRight) - height[i]. Use two pointers to avoid extra space.
approach: Two Pointer: left=0, right=n-1. Track leftMax, rightMax. If leftMax < rightMax: water += leftMax - height[left], move left++. Else: water += rightMax - height[right], move right--.

title: 3Sum
description: Given an integer array nums, return all triplets that sum to zero.
hint: Sort array. Fix one element, use two pointers for the remaining pair. Skip duplicates.
approach: Sort array O(n log n). For each i, use two pointers l=i+1, r=n-1. If sum<0: l++. If sum>0: r--. If sum==0: add triplet, skip duplicates. Total: O(n²).

title: Reverse a Linked List
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the reversed list.
hint: Use three pointers: prev=null, curr=head, next. At each step: save next, point curr to prev, move forward.
approach: Iterative: prev=null, curr=head. While curr: next=curr.next, curr.next=prev, prev=curr, curr=next. Return prev. Recursive: reverse(head.next), head.next.next=head, head.next=null.

title: LRU Cache
description: Design a data structure that follows LRU cache constraints. Implement get and put in O(1).
hint: Combine HashMap + Doubly Linked List. HashMap gives O(1) access, DLL gives O(1) insertion/deletion.
approach: HashMap stores key→node. DLL maintains order (MRU at head, LRU at tail). On get: move node to head. On put: add at head, if over capacity remove tail. Both O(1).

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: Return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path in a binary tree.
hint: At each node, max path through it = node.val + max(0, leftGain) + max(0, rightGain). Update global max.
approach: DFS postorder. For each node: leftGain = max(0, dfs(left)), rightGain = max(0, dfs(right)). Update maxSum = max(maxSum, node.val + leftGain + rightGain). Return node.val + max(leftGain, rightGain) to parent.

title: Coin Change
description: Given coin denominations and a total amount, return fewest coins needed. Return -1 if not possible.
hint: dp[i] = minimum coins to make amount i. For each amount, try all coins.
approach: Bottom-up DP: dp[0]=0, dp[i]=INF. For each amount i from 1 to amount: for each coin c: if c<=i, dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-c]+1). Answer is dp[amount] or -1 if INF.

title: Number of Islands
description: Given a 2D binary grid, return the number of islands using DFS/BFS.
hint: For each unvisited '1', do DFS/BFS to mark all connected land as visited. Count how many times you start a DFS.
approach: Iterate grid. When '1' found: increment count, DFS to mark all connected '1's as '0' (visited). DFS explores 4 directions. Time: O(M*N), each cell visited once.

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You can climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb n stairs?
hint: This is Fibonacci! ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). You either came from step n-1 or n-2.
approach: DP: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Base: dp[1]=1, dp[2]=2. Optimize space: only keep last two values. Pattern: Fibonacci sequence.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Given two strings, return the length of their longest common subsequence.
hint: If chars match: dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]. Else: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
approach: 2D DP table. dp[i][j] = LCS of text1[0..i] and text2[0..j]. If text1[i]==text2[j]: dp[i][j]=1+dp[i-1][j-1]. Else: max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Answer: dp[m][n].

title: Binary Search
description: Given a sorted array and a target, return index of target or -1.
hint: Divide search space in half each time. Compare mid element with target.
approach: left=0, right=n-1. While left<=right: mid=(left+right)/2. If nums[mid]==target: return mid. If nums[mid]<target: left=mid+1. Else: right=mid-1. Each step halves search space → O(log n).

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Given a rotated sorted array, find target in O(log n).
hint: One half is always sorted. Check which half is sorted, then decide which half to search.
approach: Binary search with extra check. At mid: if left half sorted (nums[left]<=nums[mid]): check if target in [left,mid], else search right. If right half sorted: check if target in [mid,right], else search left.

title: Rain Collector Valleys
description: Find total water trapped between terrain blocks after rain. Water at index i = min(leftMax, rightMax) - height[i].
hint: Two pointer approach: maintain leftMax and rightMax. Process from the side with smaller max.
approach: Two Pointers: left=0, right=n-1. If leftMax<rightMax: water+=leftMax-height[left], left++. Else: water+=rightMax-height[right], right--. No extra array needed → O(1) space.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description: Return total count of continuous subarrays whose sum equals k.
hint: Use prefix sum. If prefixSum[j] - prefixSum[i] = k, then subarray [i+1..j] sums to k.
approach: HashMap stores frequency of prefix sums. For each element: prefixSum += nums[i]. If (prefixSum - k) exists in map: count += map[prefixSum-k]. Add prefixSum to map. Single pass O(n).

title: Task Scheduler with Cooldown
description: Given tasks and cooldown n, find minimum intervals to finish all tasks.
hint: Most frequent task determines minimum time. Formula: (maxFreq-1)*(n+1) + countOfMaxFreq.
approach: Count frequencies. maxFreq = highest frequency. countMax = tasks with maxFreq. Answer = max(tasks.length, (maxFreq-1)*(n+1)+countMax). Greedy: schedule most frequent first, fill gaps with others or idle.

title: Word Ladder Transformation
description: Find shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord changing one letter at a time.
hint: BFS gives shortest path. At each step, try changing each character to a-z and check if it's in wordList.
approach: BFS from beginWord. For each word in queue: try all 26 chars at each position. If new word in wordSet: add to queue, remove from set (avoid revisit). Level = transformation count. M=word length, N=wordList size.

title: Maximum Profit with K Transactions
description: Find maximum profit with at most k buy-sell transactions.
hint: dp[i][j] = max profit using at most i transactions up to day j. If k >= n/2, use greedy (unlimited transactions).
approach: If k>=n/2: greedy sum of all positive differences. Else: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j-1], max over m<j of (prices[j]-prices[m]+dp[i-1][m])). Optimize with running max to reduce to O(kn).

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Find minimum window in s containing all characters of t.
hint: Expand right until all chars found. Then shrink left to minimize. Track 'formed' count to know when window is valid.
approach: Two pointers + frequency maps. Expand right: add char to window map, if freq matches t's freq increment 'formed'. When formed==required: try shrinking left. Update minWindow. Shrink until window invalid.

title: Weird Algorithm
description: Simulate the Collatz conjecture: if n is even divide by 2, if odd multiply by 3 and add 1. Print all values until n=1.
hint: Just simulate the process. No trick needed.
approach: While n != 1: if n%2==0 print n/2 else print 3n+1. Repeat.

title: Missing Number
description: Given all numbers 1 to n except one, find the missing number.
hint: Sum formula: n*(n+1)/2. Subtract actual sum to get missing number.
approach: Expected sum = n*(n+1)/2. Actual sum = sum of given array. Missing = expected - actual.

title: Repetitions
description: Given a DNA string, find the longest repetition of a single character.
hint: Track current streak and max streak while scanning.
approach: Single pass: track current char and count. When char changes, update max. Return max.

title: Increasing Array
description: Make array non-decreasing with minimum number of moves (each move increases an element by 1).
hint: Greedily increase each element to be at least as large as previous.
approach: Scan left to right. If arr[i] < arr[i-1], add (arr[i-1]-arr[i]) to moves and set arr[i]=arr[i-1].

title: Permutations
description: Construct a permutation of 1..n such that no two adjacent elements differ by 1.
hint: Print all even numbers first, then all odd numbers.
approach: Output: 2,4,6,...,1,3,5,... This ensures no two adjacent numbers differ by 1. Special case: n=1 output 1, n=2 no solution.

title: Number Spiral
description: Given row r and column c, find the number at that position in a spiral-filled grid.
hint: The diagonal element at (n,n) is n^2. Work from there based on which side of diagonal you are.
approach: Let d=max(r,c). If d is odd: if r>=c then value=d*d-(d-c), else value=d*d-(2*d-1)+(r-1). If d is even: opposite.

title: Two Knights
description: Count the number of ways to place two knights on an n x n chessboard so they don't attack each other.
hint: Total placements - attacking placements. Knights attack in 2x3 rectangles.
approach: Total = C(n^2, 2). Attacking pairs = 4*(n-1)*(n-2) for each board size k from 1 to n.

title: Two Sets
description: Divide numbers 1..n into two sets with equal sums.
hint: Total sum must be even. Greedily assign numbers to sets.
approach: If n*(n+1)/2 is odd: impossible. Else target = sum/2. Greedily pick largest numbers for set1 until target reached.

title: Bit Strings
description: Count the number of bit strings of length n.
hint: Answer is 2^n mod 10^9+7.
approach: Use fast modular exponentiation: result = pow(2, n, MOD).

title: Trailing Zeros
description: Count trailing zeros in n factorial.
hint: Count factors of 5 in n!. Each pair of 2 and 5 gives a trailing zero.
approach: ans = n/5 + n/25 + n/125 + ... until divisor > n. Factors of 2 always exceed factors of 5.

title: Tower of Hanoi
description: Print the moves to solve Tower of Hanoi with n disks.
hint: Recursively move n-1 disks to auxiliary, move largest to target, move n-1 from auxiliary to target.
approach: hanoi(n, from, to, aux): hanoi(n-1,from,aux,to), print move from->to, hanoi(n-1,aux,to,from). Total moves = 2^n - 1.

title: Creating Strings
description: Given a string, print all distinct permutations in alphabetical order.
hint: Sort string first, then use next_permutation or backtracking with visited array.
approach: Sort characters. Use backtracking: at each position try each unused character. Skip duplicates by checking if same char was used at this position before.

title: Apple Division
description: Divide n apples into two groups to minimize the difference of sums.
hint: Try all 2^n subsets. For each subset compute sum difference.
approach: For each subset S of {1..n}: diff = |sum(S) - (totalSum - sum(S))|. Track minimum diff. n<=20 so 2^20 is feasible.

title: Gray Code
description: Generate a Gray code sequence of n bits where consecutive codes differ by exactly one bit.
hint: Gray code formula: i XOR (i>>1) gives the i-th Gray code.
approach: For i from 0 to 2^n - 1: gray[i] = i ^ (i>>1). Print as binary string. Consecutive values differ by exactly 1 bit.

title: Distinct Numbers
description: Count the number of distinct values in an array.
hint: Use a set or sort and count unique elements.
approach: Insert all elements into a HashSet. Answer = set.size(). Or sort and count elements where arr[i] != arr[i-1].

title: Apartments
description: Match applicants to apartments where each applicant accepts apartments within k of their desired size.
hint: Sort both arrays. Use two pointers to greedily match.
approach: Sort applicants and apartments. Two pointers: if |apt - desired| <= k, match and advance both. If apt too small, advance apt pointer. If apt too large, advance applicant pointer.

title: Ferris Wheel
description: Pair children on a ferris wheel (max 2 per gondola) to minimize gondolas used.
hint: Sort weights. Try to pair lightest with heaviest if they fit together.
approach: Sort. Two pointers l=0, r=n-1. If weights[l]+weights[r]<=limit: pair them, l++, r--, gondolas++. Else: r alone, r--, gondolas++.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
description: Find the maximum sum of a contiguous subarray.
hint: Kadane's algorithm: track current sum and reset when negative.
approach: currentSum = max(arr[i], currentSum + arr[i]). maxSum = max(maxSum, currentSum). Kadane's algorithm in single pass.

title: Stick Lengths
description: Make all sticks the same length with minimum total cost (cost = sum of absolute differences).
hint: Optimal target length is the median. Sort and pick middle element.
approach: Sort array. Median minimizes sum of absolute deviations. Target = arr[n/2]. Cost = sum of |arr[i] - median|.

title: Playlist
description: Find the longest subarray with all distinct values (longest playlist without repeating songs).
hint: Sliding window: expand right, when duplicate found shrink left past previous occurrence.
approach: HashMap stores last index of each song. Two pointers: right expands, when duplicate at index j found: left = max(left, j+1). Window = right - left + 1.

title: Towers
description: Build towers by placing cubes: each cube goes on top of a tower where top cube is strictly larger. Minimize number of towers.
hint: Greedy: for each cube, place on tower with smallest top that is still larger than current cube.
approach: Use multiset of tower tops. For each cube x: find smallest top > x using upper_bound. If found, replace it with x. Else create new tower. Answer = multiset size.

title: Sum of Two Values
description: Find two values in array that sum to target x.
hint: HashMap: for each element check if (target - element) exists in map.
approach: HashMap approach: store index of each element. For each arr[i], check if (x - arr[i]) exists in map and index != i. Return pair of indices.

title: Factory Machines
description: Find minimum time for n machines (each with different production time) to produce t products.
hint: Binary search on answer. Check if given time T is enough: sum of floor(T/machine[i]) >= t.
approach: Binary search on time T. For given T: products = sum(T/k[i]). If products >= t: T is feasible. Find minimum feasible T.

title: Subarray Sums I
description: Count subarrays with sum exactly x (all positive numbers).
hint: Since all positive, use sliding window. Shrink when sum exceeds x.
approach: Two pointers. Expand right adding elements. When sum > x: shrink from left. When sum == x: count++, shrink left. Works because all elements positive.

title: Subarray Sums II
description: Count subarrays with sum exactly x (can have negative numbers).
hint: Prefix sum + HashMap. Count pairs where prefixSum[j] - prefixSum[i] = x.
approach: HashMap stores frequency of prefix sums. For each index: count += map[prefixSum - x]. Then add prefixSum to map. Handles negatives unlike sliding window.

title: Dice Combinations
description: Count ways to make sum n by throwing a dice (values 1-6). Answer mod 10^9+7.
hint: dp[i] = sum of dp[i-1] + dp[i-2] + ... + dp[i-6].
approach: dp[0]=1 (base). For i from 1 to n: dp[i] = sum(dp[i-j]) for j=1..6 where i-j>=0. Answer = dp[n].

title: Minimizing Coins
description: Find minimum number of coins to make sum n.
hint: Classic coin change DP. dp[i] = min coins to make sum i.
approach: dp[0]=0, dp[i]=INF. For each i: for each coin c: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-c]+1). Answer = dp[n] or -1 if INF.

title: Coin Combinations I
description: Count ordered ways to make sum n using given coins (order matters).
hint: dp[i] = number of ways to make sum i. For each sum, try all coins.
approach: dp[0]=1. For i from 1 to n: for each coin c: dp[i] += dp[i-c]. Order matters so iterate sums outer, coins inner.

title: Coin Combinations II
description: Count unordered ways to make sum n using given coins (order doesn't matter).
hint: Unbounded knapsack. Iterate coins outer, sums inner to avoid counting permutations.
approach: dp[0]=1. For each coin c: for i from c to n: dp[i] += dp[i-c]. Coin outer loop ensures each combination counted once.

title: Removing Digits
description: Repeatedly remove a digit of n from n itself. Find minimum steps to reach 0.
hint: dp[i] = min steps to reach 0 from i. For each digit d of i: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-d]+1).
approach: dp[0]=0. For i from 1 to n: for each digit d in str(i): if d>0: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-d]+1). Answer = dp[n].

title: Grid Paths I
description: Count paths from top-left to bottom-right of n x n grid moving only right or down. Some cells are blocked.
hint: dp[i][j] = paths to reach cell (i,j). dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1] if not blocked.
approach: dp[1][1]=1. For each cell: if blocked dp[i][j]=0. Else dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]. Answer = dp[n][n].

title: Edit Distance
description: Find minimum edit distance (insert, delete, replace) to convert string A to string B.
hint: dp[i][j] = edit distance between A[0..i] and B[0..j].

title: Book Shop
description: 0/1 Knapsack: maximize pages read given budget and book prices/pages.
hint: Classic 0/1 knapsack. dp[i][j] = max pages using first i books with budget j.
approach: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i-1][j-price[i]] + pages[i]). Optimize space to 1D array iterating budget backwards.

title: Increasing Subsequence
description: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
hint: Patience sorting / binary search on tails array.
approach: Maintain tails array. For each element x: binary search for first tail >= x, replace it with x. If x > all tails, append. Length of tails = LIS length.

title: Counting Rooms
description: Count the number of rooms (connected components) in a grid map where '.' is floor and '#' is wall.
hint: DFS/BFS from each unvisited '.' cell. Count how many times you start a new DFS.
approach: For each unvisited '.' cell: count++, DFS to mark all connected '.' as visited. Move in 4 directions. Answer = count.

title: Labyrinth
description: Find path from A to B in a grid maze. Print the path using directions U/D/L/R.
hint: BFS gives shortest path. Track parent of each cell to reconstruct path.
approach: BFS from A. Store parent[cell] = (prev_cell, direction). When B reached, backtrack through parents to get path. Print directions.

title: Building Roads
description: Find minimum roads to connect all cities (find connected components, connect them).
hint: Find all connected components. Need (components - 1) roads. Connect any node from each component.
approach: DFS/BFS to find connected components. Collect one representative from each component. Answer = components-1 roads connecting representatives.

title: Shortest Routes I
description: Find shortest paths from node 1 to all other nodes in a directed weighted graph.
hint: Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue.
approach: Dijkstra: dist[1]=0, all others INF. Min-heap of (dist, node). Process node: for each neighbor, if dist[node]+weight < dist[neighbor]: update and push to heap.

title: Shortest Routes II
description: Answer q queries: shortest path between nodes u and v in undirected weighted graph.
hint: Floyd-Warshall precomputes all-pairs shortest paths in O(n^3).
approach: dist[i][j] = direct edge or INF. For k,i,j: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k]+dist[k][j]). Answer each query in O(1).

title: Course Schedule
description: Given course prerequisites, find a valid order to complete all courses (topological sort).
hint: Topological sort using DFS or Kahn's algorithm (BFS with in-degree).
approach: Kahn's: compute in-degree of all nodes. Queue nodes with in-degree 0. Process: add to result, decrease neighbor in-degrees, add new 0-in-degree nodes. If result size < n: cycle exists.

title: Round Trip
description: Find a cycle in an undirected graph. Print the cycle if it exists.
hint: DFS with color marking: white=unvisited, gray=in-stack, black=done. Back edge to gray node = cycle.
approach: DFS with parent tracking. If we visit an already-visited node that isn't parent: cycle found. Backtrack to reconstruct cycle path.

title: Road Reparation
description: Find minimum spanning tree cost. If graph not connected, output IMPOSSIBLE.
hint: Kruskal's algorithm: sort edges by weight, add if doesn't create cycle using Union-Find.
approach: Sort edges. Union-Find to track components. For each edge (u,v,w): if find(u)!=find(v): union them, add w to MST cost. If MST has n-1 edges: done. Else IMPOSSIBLE.

title: Static Range Sum Queries
description: Answer q queries each asking for sum of elements in range [l, r].
hint: Precompute prefix sums. Query answer = prefix[r] - prefix[l-1].
approach: prefix[0]=0, prefix[i]=prefix[i-1]+arr[i]. For query [l,r]: answer = prefix[r] - prefix[l-1]. O(1) per query after O(n) preprocessing.

title: Dynamic Range Sum Queries
description: Support point updates and range sum queries.
hint: Use Fenwick Tree (BIT) or Segment Tree for O(log n) updates and queries.
approach: Fenwick Tree: update(i, delta): add delta to position i and propagate. query(l,r): prefix(r) - prefix(l-1). Each operation O(log n).

title: Range Xor Queries
description: Answer range XOR queries using prefix XOR.
hint: XOR has same prefix property as sum. prefix[r] XOR prefix[l-1] = XOR of range [l,r].
approach: prefix[0]=0, prefix[i]=prefix[i-1] XOR arr[i]. Query [l,r] = prefix[r] XOR prefix[l-1]. O(1) per query.

title: String Matching
description: Count occurrences of pattern in text.
hint: Use KMP or Z-algorithm for O(n+m) string matching.
approach: Z-algorithm: create string pattern+'$'+text. Z[i] = length of longest prefix of combined string matching substring starting at i. Count positions where Z[i] >= len(pattern).

title: Finding Borders
description: Find all borders of a string (prefix that is also a suffix).
hint: KMP failure function gives all border lengths.
approach: Compute KMP failure function f[]. f[i] = length of longest proper prefix of s[0..i] that is also suffix. All borders: follow chain f[n-1], f[f[n-1]-1], ... until 0.

title: Longest Palindrome
description: Find the longest palindromic substring.
hint: Manacher's algorithm finds all palindromes in O(n). Or expand around center in O(n^2).
approach: Expand around center: for each center (n centers for odd, n-1 for even length), expand while chars match. Track max length palindrome found.

title: Exponentiation
description: Compute a^b mod 10^9+7 for multiple queries.
hint: Fast power: a^b = (a^(b/2))^2 if b even, a*(a^(b-1)) if b odd.
approach: Recursive: power(a,b) = if b==0: 1. if b%2==0: x=power(a,b/2), return x*x%MOD. else: return a*power(a,b-1)%MOD. O(log b).

title: Counting Divisors
description: For each number in array, count its divisors.
hint: For each number n, iterate i from 1 to sqrt(n). If i divides n, count both i and n/i.
approach: For each x: count=0. For i=1 to sqrt(x): if x%i==0: count += (i==x/i) ? 1 : 2. O(sqrt(x)) per number.

title: Fibonacci Numbers
description: Find nth Fibonacci number mod 10^9+7.
hint: Matrix exponentiation: [[1,1],[1,0]]^n gives Fibonacci numbers.
approach: For small n: simple DP. For large n: matrix exponentiation [[1,1],[1,0]]^n. F(n) = result[0][1]. O(log n) with matrix fast power.

title: Nim Game I
description: Two players take turns removing objects from heaps. Player who takes last object wins. Determine winner.
hint: XOR of all heap sizes. If XOR != 0: first player wins. If XOR == 0: second player wins.
approach: Compute XOR of all heap sizes. If XOR != 0: first player wins (can always make XOR=0). If XOR == 0: second player wins. This is Sprague-Grundy theorem.
